newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIAN POLICE RAID SELLERS OF PIRATED CDS.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIAN POLICE RAID SELLERS OF PIRATED CDS.

text.p: Police in the Bulgarian capital on Tuesday raided vendors selling pirated compact discs and audio cassettes as part of a crackdown on the trade in which Bulgaria is second only to China.
An Interior Ministry statement said police confiscated more than 1,000 CDs and 1,500 cassettes.
Last month police checked CD-producing firms in Sofia and in Botevgrad, Veliko Tarnovo and Stara Zagora.

The interim government which took office in February vowed to crack down on audio-visual piracy and the interior ministry said on Wednesday police had seized more than 200,000 pirated CDs in the first four months of the year.
Interior Minister Bogomil Bonev will retain his post in the new cabinet to be voted on by parliament on Wednesday.
Intellectual piracy has flourished in Bulgaria with the liberalisation of its markets since the fall of communist rule in 1989.

The International Federation of the Phonographic Industry (IFPI), representing the $40 billion international recording industry, said Bulgaria was producing an estimated 15 million discs a year and five CD plants were estimated to supply about one in eight of all illegal copies on the world CD black market.
Washington put Bulgaria on a "watch list" last October and the IFPI urged the EU to block Bulgaria's accession to the World Trade Organisation until it cracked down on piracy. RDN
